content: 1. Eluxadoline and CYP2C9/10 Metabolism: Eluxadoline levels may be increased when co-administered with drugs that inhibit hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Levoketoconazole: Levoketoconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. In cases of significant interaction, consider alternative therapies. 3. OATP1B1 Inhibitors: When eluxadoline is co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg orally twice daily to mitigate the risk of increased systemic exposure. 4. Levorphanol and Eluxadoline: Co-administration may result in pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 5. Constipation Risk: Avoid co-administration of eluxadoline with other drugs that cause constipation, as this increases the risk of serious constipation-related adverse reactions. Monitor patients closely. 6. Levothyroxine: Eluxadoline increases levothyroxine levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor thyroid function. 7. Liothyronine: Eluxadoline may increase liothyronine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Loperamide: Loperamide may be used occasionally for acute management of severe diarrhea but should not be used chronically with eluxadoline. Discontinue loperamide immediately if constipation occurs. 9. Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Consider alternative therapies if necessary. 10. Lorcaserin: Lorcaserin increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Strong CYP2D6 Inhibitors: Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, exercise caution when co-administering with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 12. Lovastatin: Lovastatin increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative therapies. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg orally twice daily. 13. Mefenamic Acid: Mefenamic acid increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism.
